steps.title: The plain seven symbol
steps.body:
**dominant 7th chord** means a major triad plus a minor seventh above its root. A plain 7 after a root means this type: G7 is G, B, D and F.

**Why it matters:** G7 and Gmaj7 use different sevenths, so their written symbols must stay distinct.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: Use the G7 shape: string 6 fret 3, string 5 fret 2, strings 4, 3 and 2 open, string 1 fret 1. F3 is ten half steps above G2. This shape uses F4, the same note name one octave higher; spreading chord notes over more than one octave keeps the same chord type.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Compare the highest note of G with G7: string 1 changes from fret 3 to fret 1. Clear the taps before changing.
